description: Inventory and staged CPU/strict-CUDA validation policy for Python Meep tests and examples. Scheme is intentionally out of scope.

inventory.reason: Non-adjoint Python regression with an embedded numerical or behavioral oracle.
Example is inventoried, but a deterministic observable extractor and per-observable FP32 tolerance must be registered before claiming CPU/CUDA equivalence.
Notebook is a presentation duplicate of a same-purpose Python example and is excluded from repeated execution.

A real Meep two-segment trajectory proves that the generic oracle's intermediate whole-cell energy and DFT-norm probes do not perturb subsequent CPU or strict-CUDA fields, DFT accumulators, energy, or timestep.

Full upstream Cartesian adjoint coverage: DFT fields, eigenmodes, LDOS, complex fields, damping, anisotropy, multiple objectives/frequencies, periodic designs, resolution mapping, and gradient backpropagation.

Headless intended-semantics regression for the connectivity notebook verifies disconnected/connected reference values, conductivity-constraint gradients, an integrated damped Near2Far adjoint objective, and solid/void length-scale constraints. It deliberately corrects the notebook cell's endpoint-grid and fixed-boundary masking mistakes instead of claiming an exact replay.

A fixed high-beta slice of the published mode-converter retains six wavelengths, reflected-field subtraction, mode-1 to mode-2 conversion, damping, subpixel averaging, two objectives, the full minimax epigraph residual/Jacobian, mapped gradients, and line-width/spacing constraints without its roughly 14-hour NLopt trajectory.
Adjoint/inverse-design notebooks are validated with objective and gradient oracles in M8.

The notebook's fixed-design physics and vector epigraph Jacobian are executed headlessly by near2far_epigraph_validation.py; only its long repeated NLopt trajectory and plotting are omitted.

connectivity_validation.py executes both Phase-I reference structures and a fixed-design integration of the Near2Far objective, solid/void connectivity, and length-scale gradients using corrected endpoint-grid and fixed-boundary-mask semantics; it is an intended-semantics regression rather than an exact replay of the erroneous notebook cells.

Its single-frequency EigenmodeCoefficient objective and explicit finite-difference bend gradient are covered more broadly by test_adjoint_solver.py and the mapped waveguide_crossing.py validation slice.
This repeats the introductory eigenmode bend physics inside an NLopt trajectory; fixed-point objective and gradient coverage is provided by test_adjoint_solver.py and waveguide_crossing.py.

Its conic-filter, projection, symmetry, and multifrequency adjoint paths are covered by waveguide_crossing.py, test_adjoint_jax.py, and the mode-converter validation without repeating beta-continuation optimization.

The splitter is a filtered-bend derivative; mirror symmetry, multiple eigenmode outputs/objectives, and mapped gradients are covered by waveguide_crossing.py, test_adjoint_solver.py, and mode_converter.py.
Its bend mapping duplicates the filtered-bend notebook and its vector minimax/epigraph formulation is covered with six wavelengths and two objectives by mode_converter.py.
Its default-grid FourierFields objective is covered by test_adjoint_solver.py; its bend filter/projection mapping is covered by waveguide_crossing.py.
Its Yee-grid multi-frequency FourierFields path is covered by multilayer_opt.py while metalens vector-objective mapping and far-field physics are covered by near2far_epigraph_validation.py.

Fixed-design slices exercise C4 filtering plus smoothed/tanh projections at low and extreme beta, with mapped adjoint gradients and independent forward directional differences. A reduced two-epoch NLopt run additionally verifies callback sequencing, design mutation, beta continuation, solver reset, checkpointing, and final-result output.

test_bend_flux.py executes the same normalization/scatter pair, 100-bin flux, saved-minus incident data, and reflection/transmission physics with golden spectra, multiple DFT decimation factors, and real/complex agreement; the omitted example-only behavior is output formatting.

test_cavity_arrayslice.py uses the same cavity, source, PML, resolution, post-source time, and 1D/2D volumes and compares full arrays to FP32-aware golden data while also checking supplied-array dtype and shape behavior.

test_cyl_ellipsoid.py reproduces the Cylinder-plus-Ellipsoid geometry, PML, resolution 100, symmetry, callbacks, until=23, and probe point, checks the final Hz numerically, and additionally exercises Ez.

test_holey_wvg_cavity.py executes both the default 500-bin transmission branch and the optional resonant/Harminv branch, checking 46 spectrum pairs plus frequency, decay, Q, and amplitude; it covers the feature set without claiming every example spectrum bin.

test_oblique_source.py includes the example's default 20-degree rotated waveguide, NO_DIRECTION EigenModeSource, kpoint_func, flux, and mode coefficients and strengthens it with 0/20/40-degree flux-versus-modal-power numerical checks.
test_pw_source.py reproduces the cell, two ContinuousSource terms, phase callback, PML, resolution, and until=400 and verifies the complex field ratio at two points against the analytic phase.
test_refl_angular.py executes the same incident-normalization, saved-minus-flux, interface, and angular-reflectance workflow and checks normal, oblique, and BFAST angles against Fresnel theory.

test_ring.py reproduces the ring geometry, source, PML, resolution, symmetry, and 300-time Harminv run and numerically checks mode frequency, decay, amplitude, final field, and epsilon while adding PadeDFT coverage; the omitted example tail is an output callback over the same fields.

test_wvg_src.py reproduces the asymmetric waveguide, continuous EigenModeSource, complex fields, PML, resolution, until=200, and two flux boxes and checks both directional fluxes against golden values; only PNG/HDF5 presentation output is omitted.

The FP32-safe example executes reference and periodic-grating decay runs, compares nonzero DFT state for each run, completes all 210 MPB decompositions, and directly compares all 210 diffraction angles and transmittances. Its sole compatibility edit accepts and records only a bounded 32-FP32-epsilon direction-cosine overshoot before acos, and rejects larger physical-domain violations.

The instrumented complex oblique grating executes 20,000-step incident and 30,000-step structure runs, saved-minus flux, directly compares all 59 reflected and 39 transmitted mode powers/angles, and independently bounds both modal and Poynting energy closure.

The finite-grating field-profile branch executes flat and five-cell grating runs with symmetry/PML, independently asserts the fixed 501x352 full-field shape, and directly compares all 176,352 complex scattered-field values as well as 257 fixed-position samples and full-array summaries.

The cylindrical complex-field example executes empty-cell and dielectric-cylinder runs, three saved-minus flux boxes, and directly compares the complete 100-frequency scattering cross section and its size-parameter frequency axis.

The near2far tutorial executes its dynamic DFT-decay run, directly compares all 50x6 complex far-field amplitudes, raw and normalized radial-flux patterns, normalization scale, and analytic array, and enforces the published relative-error bound. CPU and FP32 CUDA legitimately cross the stop_when_dft_decayed threshold at different timesteps, so work/time counters use a bounded dynamic tolerance while the physical outputs remain tight. Strict CUDA validation also requires a nonzero CUDA Near2Far transform counter so host Green-transform fallback cannot satisfy the oracle.

The corrected high-Q ring example executes distinct w and 2w source/Harminv trajectories, retains the w fields object across reset, verifies both field energies and extracted frequencies, and directly compares the nonzero cross-fields integrate2 overlap result under CPU and strict CUDA.

The example executes reference/interface mode-monitor runs for both S and P total-internal-reflection polarizations, directly compares both complex reflection coefficients and analytic Fresnel coefficients, and enforces the published magnitude/phase relative-error limits. Its only instrumentation edit retains the already-printed numerical results in top-level vectors.

The example executes incident and reflected runs for all real/imag, complex, and 3d kz_2d storage modes; every DFT signal is nonzero, the three reflectances are compared directly, their spread is bounded, and each is independently gated against Fresnel theory.

The 1D tutorial executes reference and dispersive fused-quartz runs with PML, directly compares all 50 saved-minus reflectance values and wavelengths, and independently bounds every value against the analytic Sellmeier/Fresnel spectrum.

The complex-field tutorial exercises oblique EigenModeSource/MPB initialization, k-point propagation and PML, directly compares 17 x-line and 502 y-line complex Ez samples, and independently bounds the adjacent-sample Bloch phase error. The sparse 17-point trace has a local 2e-5 absolute FP32 floor (1.46e-6 of its 13.68 peak field) while the denser 502-point trace retains the stricter 1e-5 floor.

The bent-waveguide tutorial exercises two dielectric blocks, PML, a continuous source and repeated HDF5 output, then directly compares 11 complex Ez samples along the horizontal/vertical bend and an off-guide control point.
The unchanged tutorial is executed through the generic post-run oracle, comparing exact work counts and every value of its defining 160x80 Ez field under CPU FP32 and strict CUDA.

The CW ring-resonator example executes four representable FP32 solver tolerances plus the time-domain DFT reference, requires every reliable-restart solve to reach its independently recomputed true-residual target, monotonic convergence, and a final relative field error below 0.02, and directly compares both complete 242x242 CW and DFT fields. Loose-tolerance convergence-path errors are retained as diagnostic metrics because valid CPU and CUDA Krylov trajectories need not be identical; final complete fields remain gating. Its compatibility edit replaces removed NumPy np.complex_ and avoids residual requests below FP32 resolution while preserving the upstream FP64 tolerance path.

The complete published Kerr-medium workflow runs four 400-frequency spectra and a 31-point chi3 sweep. The oracle compares every spectrum and harmonic value and the source independently rejects loss of the perturbative third-harmonic power proportional to chi3 squared scaling.

The validation profile retains the full Harminv, reset, dynamically-Q-sized rerun, direct dft_ldos, and Q/V Purcell-estimate workflow for the finite-Q aperture. It compares the resonance, Q, both LDOS estimates, dynamic duration, and their independent physical closure.

The combined validation profile executes cylindrical m=+1, m=-1, and m=0 FDTD, forms both x- and z-polarized on-axis dipoles, compares every complex cylindrical near-to-far component and radial-flux point, and independently limits error against cos(theta)^2 and sin(theta)^2 radiation laws. Strict CUDA validation also requires a nonzero CUDA Near2Far transform counter so host Green-transform fallback cannot satisfy the oracle.

The complete 320k-active-cell dispersive SiO2 workflow compares every point of the 201x201 Dz, Ez, and absorbed-power-density arrays, both independently integrated powers, and a source-enforced two-percent closure between volume absorption and closed-surface flux.

The representative separation executes both MPB-derived odd and even EigenModeSource branches, compares frequencies, full flux and Maxwell-stress force monitors, and independently requires the normalized parity forces to have opposite signs. The 20-separation publication sweep remains the script default.

The bounded fixture preserves the unique extended-line Source.amp_func path without repeating the already-covered point-dipole sweep. On flat and textured Ag-backed structures it runs all 15 cosine modes, 45-degree rotations of the first two, and a 0.5-amplitude replay of modes 2 through 14. It requires a nonzero callback count for every FDTD source, retains every 16-frequency spectrum, gates the replay against the required 0.25 quadratic-flux response with a small-signal absolute floor, requires enough physically active modes and every active off-diagonal full-basis spectral pair to remain separated, closes the unitary trace, and gates M=12 versus M=15 ensemble convergence.

The bounded fixture preserves the unique Lorentz-reciprocity pair: directional ODD_Z eigenmode power from forward dipoles and a cubature-weighted backward plane-wave DFT overlap. It represents all 55 periodic source-grid samples, validates the N+3 metadata grid including machine-zero ghosts and half endpoints, directly checks translated and reflected partners, retains every raw DFT-power sample, and requires complete base and doubled-runtime forward/backward aggregates to converge before applying strict normalized textured/flat reciprocity closure in the dispersive Ag geometry.

test_ldos.TestLDOS.test_ldos_ext_eff executes the same cylindrical m=-1 and mirror-reduced 3D extraction-efficiency workflow, including signed air flux, dft_ldos F/J total power, cylindrical-versus-3D agreement, and the additional m=+1 symmetry control. Re-running the 42-trajectory presentation sweep would duplicate that stricter CPU/strict-CUDA oracle.

The deterministic branch-matrix profile preserves the resolution-50 Ag dispersive geometry while exercising method 1 and method 2 on both flat and textured surfaces. It compares all eight simulations, every 32-frequency spectrum, ensemble statistics, per-trial norms, seeds, CustomSource callback counts, and independent method/geometry-difference gates; the original 20-trial/500-frequency defaults remain unchanged.

A bounded validation profile executes the homogeneous reference, periodic unit cell with near2far nperiod replication, and explicit five-cell supercell. Complete complex 64-by-9 far fields, enhancement, frequency/angle grids, norms, and unit-cell/supercell closure are compared. Strict CUDA validation also requires a nonzero CUDA Near2Far transform counter so host Green-transform fallback cannot satisfy the oracle.

The validation sweep retains both Lorentz poles and extracts every complex Harminv mode and inferred permittivity at seven k-points using rectangular counts/offsets as an independent topology contract.
Both cylindrical parallel and perpendicular boundary-perturbation branches compare Harminv frequencies, boundary-field integrals, analytic derivatives, finite differences, and their physical closure.
Both 2D parallel and perpendicular symmetry branches compare Harminv frequencies, boundary-field integrals, analytic derivatives, finite differences, and their physical closure.

The notebook's BFAST and fixed-k reflectance paths are deterministic duplicates of test_refl_angular.py, which checks multiple angles and frequencies against Fresnel theory under strict CUDA.

A validation-only source inside the changing region drives two strict-backend trajectories: inverse-permittivity material phasing and a static-initial-material negative control. Complete epsilon and Ez/Dz grids, analytic interpolation, endpoints, and a nonzero dynamic/static field separation prove that the changing coefficient affects FDTD rather than merely host-side dielectric output.

A two-branch wrapper executes dispersive Al with both one-dimensional Absorber and PML, samples the optical carrier at about 16 points per period, retains and verdict-gates both complete 4096-point complex ringdown traces, and independently gates power decay and branch equivalence. The signed weighted trace checksum is retained as diagnostic-only because cancellation makes that synthetic summary ill-conditioned even when the complete pointwise trace and its L2/max summaries agree.

All Ex, Ey, and Ez symmetry branches execute CUDA FDTD/DFT accumulation and the resident 2D CUDA DftNear2Far.flux/get_farfield transforms for a four-sided near-to-far box, retaining complete complex fields, signed radial and tangential power, analytic dipole patterns, and three independent flux integrals. The required Near2Far CUDA counter makes host fallback a validation failure.

The checked-in four-length taper sweep executes eight CUDA-FDTD/DFT runs with EigenModeSource and flux-data subtraction. Gauge-invariant MPB magnitudes and both reflectance definitions are checked against an independent FP64 CPU vector, together with monotonic decrease and the leading inverse-square doubling trend; currently host-side MPB solves are compatibility rather than GPU-acceleration coverage.

Normal and oblique Bloch branches execute CUDA FDTD/DFT homogeneous references and gratings, map currently host-side MPB bands to physically sorted signed diffraction orders, and retain every mode amplitude, power, group velocity, wavevector, and flux closure for both public APIs. Independent order-to-ky, outgoing-kx, vacuum-dispersion, and group-velocity gates prevent common-mode decomposition errors; host MPB work is compatibility rather than GPU-acceleration coverage.

The validation branch executes the original complex CustomSource in CUDA FDTD, retains complete complex traces at six spatial probes, and independently checks the source envelope, down-chirped instantaneous frequency, vacuum transit delay, propagated waveform, and transverse planewave uniformity.

The validation branch executes complete symmetric superluminal, symmetric subthreshold, and unsymmetrized superluminal moving-source trajectories plus an independent resolution-doubled superluminal convergence run in CUDA FDTD. It retains all nine base-resolution full-domain Hz snapshots, the complete 800x800 resolution-doubled Hz snapshot, and all three source tracks; independently checks Mirror(Y) reconstruction; and gates trajectory velocity, physical symmetry, wake energy, a source-excluded fitted spectral ridge against the discrete Yee dispersion law, convergence toward continuum phase matching, inferred speed, and separation from the subthreshold negative control.

The validation branch executes the photonic-crystal cavity with a three-component direct DFT line and the surrounding 2D CUDA Near2Far monitor, then compares every complex Ex/Ey/Hz sample, component magnitude, combined intensity, signed Poynting profile, and integrated outward flux. The required Near2Far CUDA counter rejects host transformation fallback.

The validation branch executes a fixed m=0..8 cylindrical sweep for both off-axis x and y dipoles, retaining all positive/negative-frequency E/H Near2Far fields, every modal and cumulative signed/tangential Poynting pattern, analytic dipole patterns, three consecutive power-tail modes, and a final-extra-mode convergence check. All 18 cylindrical FDTD/DFT trajectories and the cylindrical Green transforms must dispatch to CUDA, enforced by the required Near2Far counter.

The validation branch performs four real 3D simulations: Ex, Ey, and Ez dipoles plus a larger-z Ex convergence control. It retains complete five-frequency emitted flux, LDOS F/J/data, each of three air-face fluxes, extraction efficiency, exact combined-versus-individual monitor additivity, work counters, source-polarization separation, and z-size convergence; every executed FDTD and DFT/LDOS accumulation phase must dispatch without CPU fallback. This nondispersive case does not claim coverage of the dispersive-material polarization updater. Monitor additivity is an API consistency check, not an independent energy-conservation law.

The bounded validation profile executes the genuine 3D rectangular supercell for a triangular-lattice grating, retains every propagating DiffractedPlanewave amplitude, power, group velocity, and wavevector, and independently enforces vacuum dispersion plus suppression of the forbidden odd supercell orders. The host MPB decomposition is compatibility coverage while the full 3D FDTD/DFT trajectory must use CUDA without fallback.

A bounded seven-geometry sweep executes spatially varying rotated off-diagonal anisotropic tensors for homogeneous and twisted-nematic polarization gratings. It retains both polarization-family magnitudes and all five mode powers at three phase delays, checks the published uniaxial cos-squared/sin-squared law, and adds a matched-thickness control which isolates director twist from thickness. MPB mode extraction is host compatibility work; all fourteen FDTD/DFT trajectories must dispatch to CUDA without fallback.

The bounded cylindrical m=-1 validation keeps the circularly polarized Er/Ep source, binary phase-zone geometry, two-surface CUDA Near2Far monitor, and complete radial/axial six-component far fields. It directly checks all complex fields and intensities plus independent focal position and contrast; the required Near2Far CUDA counter rejects Green-transform fallback.

The bounded validation preserves both the cylindrical m=-1 and mirror-reduced 3D LDOS formulations, executes bulk plus three lossless-metal cavity thicknesses in each coordinate system, and compares both Purcell-factor branches with the independent analytic result. The eight small trajectories are a numerical compatibility fixture rather than a forced-CUDA speed claim; automatic dispatch should keep launch-dominated work on CPU while larger isolated 3D cases establish production acceleration.

test_gaussianbeam.py exercises the same Gaussian-beam source geometry with the harder -40-degree propagation case, both GaussianBeam2DSource and GaussianBeam3DSource implementations, full-cell complex DFT fields, and a greater-than-0.98 focus-energy oracle under CPU and strict CUDA. The example's zero-angle continuous-source plot is a deterministic presentation subset and is not rerun.

The bounded eight-trajectory Brillouin-zone integration retains PEC ground-plane boundaries, oblique complex-k 1D propagation, PML, flux normalization at the analytic lobe maximum, and seven resolved polar samples. It compares the normalized radiation pattern directly with the independent two-element-array law. These launch-dominated trajectories are strict-CUDA correctness fixtures and should remain on CPU under automatic dispatch.

The bounded 7x8 angular sweep executes each of 33 unique complex-k 1D Ex trajectories inside the light cone once, retains the complete raw and normalized grid, and compares it with the independent x-dipole sin-squared radiation law. One off-axis Ey trajectory additionally checks the y-polarization branch and rotational symmetry. The small trajectories are strict-CUDA correctness fixtures and should remain on CPU in automatic mode.

test_holey_wvg_bands.py executes both branches of this tutorial: the same geometry and 21-point interpolated run_k_points grid in a shorter bounded trajectory with complex-frequency checks, plus a fixed-k Harminv trajectory with twelve modal frequency/decay oracles. Re-running the presentation script would duplicate those stricter CPU/strict-CUDA regression paths.

test_ring_cyl.py executes the same cylindrical m=3 dielectric-ring Harminv workflow and checks frequency, decay, Q, and complex amplitude against six reference values. Its reduced resolution/PML is a stricter bounded CPU/strict-CUDA numerical oracle; the example's trailing HDF5 field movie is presentation output rather than an additional accelerated solver path.

This script performs only NumPy normalization and Matplotlib rendering of the dipole_in_vacuum_1D output; it imports no Meep module and has no FDTD, DFT, adjoint, or GPU-compute path. The producer's full raw/normalized angular arrays and analytic error are validated by the dipole_in_vacuum_1D oracle.

The bounded fixture executes both Hz/even-z and Ez/odd-z mirror-parity branches for three duty cycles and seven frequencies. It retains all eigenmode transmissions and wrap-safe phase phasors, enforces passive power flow, and requires nontrivial duty-cycle and polarization response. Its launch-dominated unit cells are strict-CUDA correctness probes and should remain on CPU under automatic dispatch.

The bounded fixture preserves the complete unit-cell-to-lens workflow: nine eigenmode transmission/phase solves drive 121-cell and 301-cell phase profiles, followed by two near-to-far FDTD trajectories and 60-point axial focus scans. It retains raw and normalized far fields, peak positions, offsets, contrast, and phase coverage. The two lens sizes straddle the automatic local-cell crossover so production dispatch can avoid small-workload CUDA while accelerating the larger solve. Strict CUDA validation also requires a nonzero CUDA Near2Far transform counter so host Green-transform fallback cannot satisfy the oracle.

The bounded cylindrical m=-1 oracle retains every complex E/H far-field component on a 48-point quarter-circle, Cartesian and signed/magnitude radial Poynting components, near-surface and far-field integrated flux, work metadata, and independent near/far closure plus radiative H/E checks. Cylindrical FDTD, DFT accumulation, and the Green transform must dispatch to CUDA, with the Near2Far counter making fallback a failure.

The bounded 2D real/imag kz oracle executes fourteen fixed Brillouin-zone samples for each Ex/Ey/Ez source. It retains complete emitted/air flux, LDOS F/J/data, three individual boundary-face fluxes, integrated extraction efficiencies, work counters, and independent light-cone tail, source-tail, monitor-additivity, and polarization-separation checks. Every one of the 42 FDTD/DFT trajectories must use strict CUDA without fallback.

The bounded finite-disc oracle preserves the on-axis m=-1 source and four radial source positions with every fixed m=0..14 contribution. It retains all complex E/H far fields, signed/magnitude radial flux, LDOS F/J/data, modal/position/total powers, original radial quadrature, extraction efficiency, work counters, and independent modal-tail, radiative-impedance, outward-power, and radial-variation gates across 61 strict-backend trajectories. Strict CUDA validation also requires a nonzero CUDA Near2Far transform counter so host Green-transform fallback cannot satisfy the oracle.
